text:
Most visitors leave Kyoto with a box of yatsuhashi. The food hall inside Kyoto Station keeps something else for Saturday mornings: ohagi from a Kyoto sweet shop that arrive once a week, three for ¥721 👇

🎯 Classic or local? Bet you can't guess all five pairs 👉 https://japanbystation.com/kyoto-station-depachika-gifts

We went through the three department-store food halls (JR Kyoto Isetan, Daimaru and Takashimaya) and checked every price and arrival day against the stores' own lists.

🍡 THREE PAIRS FROM THE GUIDE

1️⃣ Yatsuhashi vs Saturday ohagi. All three big yatsuhashi makers have counters in JR Kyoto Isetan's B1, inside the station. On Saturdays from 11:00, the same floor gets Imanishiken's ohagi.

2️⃣ Matcha everything vs a Kyoto-only yokan. Tsuruya Yoshinobu's Kyoto-limited yokan (3 bars ¥1,274) is sold only in Kyoto and keeps for about a year. A gift that survives a long flight.

3️⃣ Station bento vs a Kyoto restaurant's box. Isetan's B2 carries bento from about 27 long-established restaurants, and Izuu's mackerel sushi is there too.

🚄 OUT OF TIME?

ASTY Square sits right in front of the Shinkansen central gate, with 551 Horai and Kyoto dango.

Our take: go down to Isetan B1 before your train, on a Saturday if you can, and buy one box to travel and one to eat today.
